intro_html: A weeknight-friendly mole: charred poblanos, onion, and peanuts blended into a deep, smoky sauce over tender chicken thighs and rice. Each bowl delivers 52 grams of protein at 560 calories for about $2.74 (at everyday cost). Poblanos and peanuts are doing work here that usually takes a restaurant kitchen all afternoon.
cost_closing_html: About $2.74 a bowl (at everyday cost) for real mole flavor over rice. A mole plate at a Mexican restaurant typically runs $13 to $16, and this batch feeds you all week for a fraction of eating out.
shop_smart: Chicken thighs beat breasts here twice: they cost less per pound and they stay juicy through the long simmer and the fridge week.
Poblanos are the flavor backbone at about $4.25 for what this batch needs. They are usually the cheapest fresh chile on the wall, and charring them is free flavor.
A small handful of peanuts from a $2.58 jar replaces the pricey nuts and seeds a traditional mole calls for. The jar covers several batches.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Char the poblanos under the broiler or over a burner flame until blistered all over. Steam them in a covered bowl 10 minutes, then peel, seed, and roughly chop.
Cook the rice: 4.75 cups dry rice in your rice cooker or a covered pot while the sauce comes together.
In your big pot, saute the chopped onion and jalapeno until soft. Add the chili powder, garlic powder, oregano, and black pepper and toast 1 minute.
Blend the poblanos, onion mixture, peanuts, and about half the chicken broth until smooth. Pour the sauce back into the pot with the rest of the broth.
Cut the chicken thighs into large chunks, season with salt, and simmer them in the sauce 20 to 25 minutes until they reach 165 F and the sauce has thickened.
Portion rice into 14 containers, ladle chicken and mole sauce over, and finish with chopped cilantro.
portion_html: Weigh the finished pot, subtract the empty pot weight you wrote down, and divide by 14 for the chicken and sauce. Split the rice evenly underneath. Each bowl lands at about 560 calories with 52 grams of protein.

steps: Char, steam, peel, and chop the poblanos; start the rice.
Saute onion and jalapeno, then toast the spices.
Blend poblanos, onion mixture, peanuts, and broth into a smooth sauce.
Simmer chunked chicken thighs in the sauce to 165 F until thickened.
Portion rice into 14 containers, top with mole chicken, and add cilantro.
